title: US-Brokered Talks Continue Over Israeli Withdrawal From Southern Lebanon
content:
Lebanon and Israel resumed direct negotiations in Rome, a meeting brokered by the United States after earlier talks in Washington that produced a framework agreement. The framework calls for the disarmament of Hezbollah and a phased withdrawal of Israeli forces from southern Lebanon, aiming to reduce tensions along the 200‑kilometre border.

The new round of talks follows the earlier Washington negotiations, where both sides agreed to the same disarmament and withdrawal plan. Hezbollah’s chief, however, rejected the Rome discussions, labeling them a humiliation for Lebanon and refusing to participate. The U.S. has continued to mediate, urging both parties to adhere to the agreed framework and to move forward with implementation steps.

The Rome talks represent a renewed attempt to solidify the framework’s provisions, though the lack of Hezbollah’s engagement remains a significant obstacle. If the parties can maintain momentum, the agreement could pave the way for a more stable security situation in the region.
author: France 24

title: Ghana Law Threatens 20-Year Prison for Cocoa Farmers
content:
Ghana’s parliament approved a new bill on July 30 that would criminalise the conversion of cocoa farms into other land uses without government consent. The legislation, which was not released to the public until August 2, grants all cocoa farms protected status and imposes prison sentences of up to 20 years for farmers who re‑purpose their plots without official approval.  

The measure, aimed at safeguarding the country’s cocoa sector, would make any unauthorized change of use a criminal offence. It has drawn sharp criticism from cocoa growers, who argue that the law restricts their ability to adapt to market pressures and manage land sustainably. Critics contend that the bill could undermine the livelihoods of thousands of small‑holder farmers who rely on cocoa production for income.  

If enacted, the law would represent a significant tightening of land‑use regulation in Ghana’s most important agricultural export. Stakeholders now await the government’s next steps, including potential amendments or implementation guidelines that could address farmers’ concerns.
author: France 24

title: Biya Reshuffles Military Leadership Amid Absence Speculation
content:
President Paul Biya of Cameroon announced a significant reshuffle of senior military leadership on August 3, issuing three separate presidential decrees that elevated the head of the Presidential Guard to the rank of brigadier general and replaced commanders in four of the country’s five joint military regions. The decrees, signed in the capital, aim to strengthen the command structure amid ongoing security challenges across the nation.

Biya, who has been in office since 1982 and is the world’s oldest serving head of state, has not appeared in public since June 7. The appointments are part of a broader effort to consolidate military control and respond to regional instability, with the new commanders expected to oversee operations in their respective regions. The changes come at a time when Cameroon faces internal unrest and cross-border threats, prompting the government to tighten its security apparatus.
author: France 24

title: DR Congo to Open Largest Ebola Treatment Facility Amid Growing Outbreak
content:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo is on the brink of opening its largest Ebola treatment facility, a move aimed at bolstering the country’s response to a rapidly expanding outbreak. Construction of the new complex is nearing completion, and health authorities are racing to bring it online as the World Health Organization (WHO) warns that the epidemic is intensifying at an “exceptional” pace.

According to WHO data released on July 30, the outbreak has already produced 3,605 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,587 deaths in the DR Congo. The expanded facility is expected to increase treatment capacity, improve patient care, and support contact tracing and community outreach efforts. Officials emphasize that the new center will be a critical component in curbing transmission and reducing mortality as the virus continues to spread across affected regions.

With the new treatment center poised to open, health officials hope the enhanced infrastructure will strengthen containment measures and provide timely care for those infected. The international community remains closely monitoring the situation, underscoring the importance of swift, coordinated action to mitigate the outbreak’s impact.
author: France 24

title: Rwanda's first Cannes Caméra d'Or win fuels local film boom
content:
Rwandan cinema entered an unprecedented spotlight in May when Marie‑Clémentine Dusabejambo’s feature film *Ben’Imana* captured the prestigious Caméra d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival, marking the first time a Rwandan production has received the award. The historic win has drawn international attention to the nation’s burgeoning film industry and underscored the artistic potential of its storytellers.

In Kigali, the momentum is evident through a series of developments: a restored movie theatre now screens both classic and contemporary works, an open‑air festival showcases local talent to growing audiences, and a new generation of filmmakers is emerging, inspired by the global recognition. The combined effect of these initiatives signals a vibrant revival of Rwandan cinema, positioning the country as an increasingly influential player on the world stage.
author: France 24

title: FIFA officials criticize Infantino's scrapped World Cup stake sale plan
content:
Gianni Infantino, FIFA’s president, is facing renewed criticism after two senior officials – secretary‑general Mattias Grafström and chief of global football development Arsène Wenger – publicly denounced his abandoned proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup. The plan, which had been floated earlier this year as a means to generate additional revenue for the sport, was subsequently scrapped amid concerns about its impact on the tournament’s integrity and commercial independence. Grafström and Wenger’s remarks have revived debate within the governing body over the president’s strategic direction and governance style.

The backlash arrives at a time when Infantino, who had been expected to run unopposed, may encounter fresh challenges in his bid for a fourth term at the FIFA congress scheduled for March. Critics argue that the failed stake‑sale episode underscores broader governance issues and could embolden potential rivals. As the election approaches, the controversy may influence member associations’ assessments of Infantino’s leadership, adding uncertainty to what had been presumed a straightforward re‑election. (Story by Laurent Berstecher)
author: France 24

title: Russian overnight missile strike kills at least two in Kyiv
content:
At least two people were killed and a dozen more injured in a Russian missile strike on Kyiv overnight, marking the latest in a series of attacks that have repeatedly tested the Ukrainian capital’s air‑defence systems. The assault, which involved both missiles and drones, struck residential areas and caused significant damage to infrastructure, prompting emergency services to evacuate the wounded to nearby hospitals. Ukrainian officials confirmed the casualties and said that the strike was part of a broader pattern of intensified Russian aerial operations aimed at undermining civilian morale and disrupting daily life in the city.

The Kyiv attack comes after several weeks of sustained Russian missile and drone bombardments that have strained Ukraine’s defensive capabilities, while Kyiv has simultaneously escalated its own long‑range strikes against targets inside Russia. Both sides have reported a growing number of civilian and military victims as the conflict expands beyond the front lines. International observers noted the escalation underscores the difficulty of containing the hostilities and the heightened risk of further civilian casualties as the war continues.
author: France 24

title: Versailles Royal Chapel Opens to Public Until September 27
content:
The royal chapel at the Palace of Versailles, newly restored after several years of work, has opened to the public for general visitation for the first time, with the temporary exhibition scheduled to run through September 27. The initiative expands access beyond the chapel’s traditional private functions, allowing visitors to experience the historic space and its ornate décor without prior appointment. 

In addition to the chapel, the palace’s ancillary annexes will showcase a collection of classical artworks until the end of the month, offering a broader cultural program for tourists and scholars alike. The opening was reported by FRANCE 24 correspondents Luke Shrago, Lilou Bernoville and Louis‑Malo Rendu, who highlighted the significance of the restoration in preserving Versailles’ heritage while enhancing its public offering.
author: France 24

title: Mexico's top university orders 58,000 students to retake entrance exam in person
content:
Mexico’s National Autonomous University (UNAM), the nation’s largest and most prestigious higher‑education institution, announced that approximately 58,000 applicants will be required to retake the entrance examination in person. The decision follows a “debacle” with the university’s first fully remote test, during which unusually high scores triggered suspicions of widespread cheating and led to the annulment of thousands of results.

UNAM stated that the forthcoming exam will be administered at designated centers under strict supervision to ensure integrity. Officials emphasized that the move aims to restore confidence in the selection process and to provide a fair assessment for all candidates. The university has not disclosed a specific date for the in‑person test, but it affirmed that the new format will replace the problematic online version for the current admission cycle.
author: Guardian World

title: UN warns El Niño could push 50 million into acute hunger by next year
content:
The United Nations’ latest food‑security outlook warns that conditions are set to deteriorate in 45 countries currently classified as experiencing severe food insecurity. Forecasts indicate that the rapidly developing El Niño weather pattern could push an additional 50 million people into acute hunger before the end of next year, compounding an already dire situation across vulnerable regions.

The surge in hunger risk comes on top of hundreds of millions who are already confronting dangerous levels of food scarcity, a crisis driven by prolonged droughts in parts of Africa and heightened food‑price pressures linked to the ongoing war in Iran. The UN urges governments and humanitarian agencies to accelerate assistance and strengthen resilience measures to avert a further escalation of the global hunger emergency.
author: Guardian World

title: Japan launches US Tomahawk missile from warship on July 29
content:
Japan conducted a test launch of a U.S.-made Tomahawk cruise missile from the destroyer JS Chōkai on July 29, firing the weapon over the Pacific Ocean. The exercise marked the first time the Japanese Maritime Self‑Defense Force has deployed the long‑range, land‑attack missile from a warship, demonstrating the integration of the system into its existing arsenal.

The trial is part of a broader effort to enhance Japan’s strike capabilities and deepen interoperability with U.S. forces, following recent agreements that allow the transfer of Tomahawk missiles to Japanese platforms. Defense officials noted that the successful launch confirms the missile’s compatibility with Japan’s ship‑board launch systems and underscores the country’s commitment to bolstering its deterrence posture in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi hits severe turbulence, 17 injured
content:
An Air India flight traveling from Phuket, Thailand, to Delhi, India, encountered severe turbulence that left seventeen passengers injured. The incident occurred mid‑flight, prompting the cabin crew to secure the cabin and administer first‑aid measures before the aircraft was able to land safely.

The turbulence, described by the airline as “unexpected and intense,” caused passengers who were not seated to be thrown about the cabin, resulting in a range of injuries from minor bruises to more serious conditions requiring medical attention. Upon landing at Indira Gandhi International Airport, the injured were transferred to nearby hospitals for treatment, while the remaining passengers were deplaned. Air India issued a statement confirming that the aircraft sustained no structural damage and that a thorough investigation has been launched in coordination with Indian aviation authorities to determine the cause of the turbulence and assess any procedural implications.

The airline reiterated its commitment to passenger safety and noted that all crew members followed established protocols for turbulence events. Officials indicated that the investigation’s findings will be used to enhance safety measures on future flights, while the flight continued to its scheduled destination after the medical response was completed.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Cape Verde forward Vozinha signs with Chilean club Colo-Colo
content:
Cape Verde goalkeeper Josimar “Vozinha” Dias, who recently signed with Chilean giants Colo‑Colo, said the transfer confirmed his long‑standing belief that he belongs at a “big club.” The 33‑year‑old, who has earned more than 50 caps for the Cape Verde national team and previously played for clubs in Portugal, Angola and Brazil, joined Colo‑Colo on a two‑year contract during the summer transfer window. In a post‑match interview, Vozinha explained that the move to the Santiago‑based side, which has won 33 domestic titles, validates his personal ambition and reflects his consistent performances at both club and international levels.

Colo‑Colo’s sporting director highlighted Vozinha’s experience and leadership as key assets for the team’s defensive line, noting that his arrival adds depth ahead of the upcoming Copa Sudamericana and domestic league campaigns. The goalkeeper’s debut is expected in the next round of fixtures, where he will compete for the starting role with incumbent keeper. His signing marks the latest high‑profile acquisition for the Chilean club as it seeks to reinforce its squad for a season targeting both national and continental success.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump says progress with Iran but warns of hard hit if no deal
content:
Washington – President Donald Trump told reporters on Thursday that his administration had made “significant progress” in talks with Iran aimed at resolving longstanding disputes over the latter’s nuclear program. The president said the United States had engaged in a series of diplomatic exchanges that have reduced tensions and opened a path toward a comprehensive agreement, though he did not specify the exact milestones achieved. Trump emphasized that the progress was the result of “strong, decisive action” by his team and highlighted the willingness of both sides to explore a framework that could lift some sanctions in exchange for verifiable limits on Iran’s uranium enrichment activities.

At the same time, Trump warned that if Tehran fails to reach a final deal, the United States will impose a “hard hit” on the Iranian economy. He indicated that additional sanctions could be reinstated or expanded, targeting key sectors such as oil exports and financial institutions. The president’s remarks come amid ongoing international efforts, led by the European Union, to bring Iran back to the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, and underscore the administration’s dual strategy of encouraging negotiation while maintaining pressure to ensure compliance.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Democratic Rift Over Israel Emerges in Michigan, Missouri, Washington Primaries
content:
Recent primary contests across the United States have highlighted a growing split within the Democratic Party over the nation’s policy toward Israel. In races ranging from New York’s 10th congressional district to California’s 13th Senate seat, progressive challengers have campaigned on platforms that call for a reassessment of U.S. military aid to Israel and an end to unconditional support, while centrist incumbents and establishment figures have defended the longstanding alliance, arguing that it is essential to U.S. strategic interests and regional stability.

The intra‑party debate has been amplified by the ongoing Israel‑Hamas conflict, which has prompted heightened scrutiny of American foreign‑policy decisions. Candidates such as Rep. Jamaal Bowman and State Sen. Alex Padilla have faced primary opponents who cite the humanitarian toll in Gaza as a reason to condition aid, whereas figures like Rep. Jerrold Nadler and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer have reiterated commitments to Israel’s security. Party leaders warn that the rift could influence voter turnout and shape the Democratic agenda ahead of the 2024 presidential election, underscoring the challenge of reconciling divergent views on a core foreign‑policy issue.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bangladesh ex-PM Sheikh Hasina expected to announce return from exile
content:
Dhaka – Khaleda Zia, the former prime minister and leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, is expected to announce her return to Bangladesh from exile in New Delhi despite a death‑penalty verdict pending against her in a high‑profile corruption case. Zia, who was released from prison in 2022 after serving a five‑year sentence for graft, fled to India amid concerns for her safety and has remained abroad while her legal team challenges the death‑sentence ruling issued by a lower court in 2023. The announcement, anticipated in a televised statement later this week, would mark her first public move toward re‑entering the country since the verdict was confirmed.

The death‑penalty case stems from allegations that Zia was involved in the 1992 murder of a political rival, a charge the ruling Awami League government has pursued vigorously as part of a broader crackdown on opposition figures. International human‑rights groups have called for a fair trial and expressed alarm over the use of capital punishment in politically sensitive cases. Bangladesh’s Election Commission has scheduled national elections for early next year, and Zia’s potential return could reshape the electoral landscape, intensifying competition between the BNP and the incumbent Awami League.

If Zia proceeds with her return, she will likely face immediate arrest and detention pending appeal of the death sentence, a scenario that could trigger widespread protests and further strain Bangladesh’s political climate. Authorities have indicated that any legal proceedings will follow due process, while opposition supporters view her comeback as a rallying point for dissent. The development underscores the ongoing tension between Bangladesh’s ruling party and its principal opposition ahead of the upcoming elections.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russian missile and drone strike kills 17 in Ukraine
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported that Russian forces deployed 29 missiles and 115 drones in a recent assault on Ukrainian territory. The strike, which Zelenskyy described as part of an intensified campaign, targeted multiple locations across the country and was announced during a televised briefing on the ongoing conflict.

The president’s statement underscores the scale of the aerial offensive and highlights Kyiv’s continued efforts to document and respond to Russian attacks. Ukrainian officials said they are assessing damage and civilian impact while coordinating defensive measures. The report adds to a series of recent disclosures about the intensity of Russian missile and drone operations in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Chad le Clos reports home destroyed by fire during Commonwealth Games
content:
South African Olympic swimming champion Chad le Clos confirmed that his family home was completely destroyed by a fire on Tuesday, while he was competing at the Commonwealth Games in Birmingham. The 27‑year‑old, a gold‑medalist from the 2012 London Olympics and multiple Commonwealth champion, was in the athletes’ village when the blaze broke out at his residence in Cape Town.

Le Clos said emergency services arrived promptly but the structure was beyond rescue, leaving his family without shelter and personal belongings. He expressed gratitude for the swift response of the fire department and noted that the incident would not affect his focus on the Games, where he is slated to race in the 100‑metre butterfly and 200‑metre individual medley. Authorities are investigating the cause of the fire, and local officials have pledged assistance to the le Clos family as they begin the recovery process.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Afghan boxer appears in court over Scottish woman's death
content:
Sharif Ahmadzai, 26, is being held by police in connection with the death of Elisabeth Jane Ross, a resident of Edinburgh. The authorities confirmed that Ahmadzai was taken into custody following an investigation that linked him to the fatal incident, though they have not disclosed the specific circumstances surrounding the case. Ross’s death has prompted a formal inquiry, and officials have indicated that the investigation remains ongoing.

Law enforcement officials have stated that Ahmadzai is currently being questioned and that further details will be released as the inquiry progresses. No additional information about potential charges or the timeline of events has been made public. The investigation continues to seek clarity on the circumstances of Ross’s death, and authorities have urged anyone with relevant information to come forward.
author: BBC World

title: Perez Hilton hospitalized after self‑harm incident, now recovering
content:
Miami police announced to U.S. media outlets that the well‑known celebrity blogger, who had been reported missing earlier this week, was “safely recovered” from his residence. The statement, released late Thursday, confirmed that officers entered the home after receiving a welfare check request and found the individual unharmed, ending a brief period of public concern and speculation.

Authorities indicated that the recovery was part of an ongoing investigation into the circumstances that led to the initial report of the blogger’s disappearance. While no further details were disclosed, police said they would continue to assess the situation and provide updates as appropriate. The incident underscores the rapid response capabilities of Miami law‑enforcement agencies in handling welfare inquiries involving high‑profile figures.
author: BBC World

title: Total Solar Eclipse Approaches Europe and Greenland
content:
**Total Solar Eclipse Looms on the Horizon**

In just one week, the United States will witness a rare and awe-inspiring spectacle: a total solar eclipse. On August 12, a narrow path of totality will stretch from Oregon to South Carolina, offering a brief but breathtaking moment of totality to millions of Americans. The eclipse will be the first total solar eclipse visible from the contiguous United States since 2017, and astronomers and skywatchers alike are eagerly anticipating the event.

The path of totality, which spans approximately 2,500 miles, will include several major cities, including Portland, Oregon; Kansas City, Missouri; and Charleston, South Carolina. During the eclipse, the moon will pass directly between the Earth and the sun, blocking the sun's light and revealing the sun's ethereal corona. The eclipse will last for approximately 4 minutes and 26 seconds at its peak, providing a fleeting glimpse of the sun's majestic beauty. Scientists will also be using the eclipse to gather valuable data on the sun's corona and the Earth's atmosphere.

As the nation prepares for the eclipse, officials are urging citizens to take necessary precautions to ensure a safe viewing experience. This includes wearing specialized solar viewing glasses or handheld solar viewers that meet international safety standards. With the right equipment and precautions, millions of Americans will be able to witness this rare and awe-inspiring event, making it a truly unforgettable experience.
author: Space.com

title: Mummy Film Ad Banned in London
content:
A controversy has emerged surrounding the promotional posters for Lee Cronin's upcoming horror film, The Mummy. The posters, which feature a depiction of a dead child, have been criticized for being "too realistic". This has sparked concerns among some members of the public, who feel that the imagery is too graphic and disturbing, particularly for a film that may appeal to a younger audience.

The posters have been displayed in various locations, including public transportation hubs and shopping centers, where they can be easily seen by people of all ages. While the intention behind the posters was likely to generate buzz and excitement for the film, some have argued that they cross a line in terms of taste and sensitivity. The use of a dead child as a promotional image has been deemed insensitive and potentially traumatic for some viewers, particularly children who may be exposed to the posters without parental guidance.

The controversy surrounding the posters serves as a reminder of the importance of considering the potential impact of marketing materials on the public, particularly when it comes to sensitive or disturbing content. As the release of The Mummy approaches, it will be interesting to see how the film's promoters respond to these concerns and whether they will make any changes to their marketing strategy to address the issue.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Carlos Alcaraz Withdraws from Cincinnati Open
content:
Carlos Alcaraz, the world's second-ranked tennis player, has withdrawn from the upcoming ATP Masters 1000 event in Cincinnati due to a persistent wrist injury. The Spaniard has been out of action since April, when he was forced to pull out of the Barcelona Open during the second round. His decision to skip the Cincinnati Open, an event he won last year, raises concerns about his preparedness for the US Open, which is scheduled to take place later this month.

Alcaraz's wrist injury has been a lingering issue, and his inability to recover in time for the Cincinnati Open may impact his chances of defending his US Open title. The 20-year-old tennis star has been working towards a comeback, but it appears that he is not yet ready to return to competitive play. The Cincinnati Open is a key tournament in the lead-up to the US Open, and Alcaraz's absence will be felt in the men's draw. As the tennis world waits for his return, Alcaraz will likely continue to work on his rehabilitation in an effort to regain his fitness and form.

The withdrawal of Alcaraz from the Cincinnati Open will undoubtedly be a significant blow to the tournament, which has lost one of its top attractions. However, the focus will now shift to the Spaniard's recovery and his prospects of returning to the court in time for the US Open. With the tennis world watching, Alcaraz will be under pressure to regain his fitness and defend his title, but for now, his priority will be to overcome his wrist injury and get back to full strength.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England Rugby Expecting £10m Loss
content:
The Rugby Football Union (RFU) is expecting a significant financial loss due to England's poor performance in the Six Nations men's competition. The team, led by Steve Borthwick, finished fifth in the table, losing four out of five matches, which is considered England's worst performance in the tournament. This disappointing outcome has resulted in reduced prize money, contributing to the RFU's anticipated £10m loss in the financial year ending June 2026.

Insiders have pointed to the team's relatively light calendar as a significant factor in their poor performance. However, the RFU has described the campaign as "hugely disappointing," indicating that the team's results were not acceptable. The financial impact of this performance will likely be felt by the RFU, which will need to adjust its budget accordingly. The loss of £10m is a substantial amount, and the RFU will need to reassess its financial strategy to mitigate the effects of this deficit.

The RFU's expected financial loss serves as a stark reminder of the high stakes involved in professional rugby. The financial consequences of a poor performance can be severe, and the RFU will need to carefully evaluate its approach to the sport to prevent similar losses in the future. As the RFU looks to the future, it will be crucial to learn from the mistakes of the past season and work towards improving the team's performance to avoid further financial setbacks.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Rashford to Return to Man Utd Training
content:
Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford is expected to resume training with the first team in the coming days, signaling a potential shift in his availability for the club’s upcoming fixtures. The England international has been separated from recent squad sessions following a period of inconsistent performances and tactical reassessments by the coaching staff. His anticipated return has prompted discussion among pundits, supporters, and media outlets regarding the timing and potential implications of his reintroduction to competitive matchday plans.

Rashford’s training absence coincided with a broader evaluation of his role within the squad as United sought to address a sustained decline in attacking output. Coaches have reportedly focused on positional adjustments and targeted conditioning to restore his match fitness and decision-making on the pitch. While some analysts suggest that bringing Rashford back into the fold could provide immediate offensive depth, others argue that continued isolated work or a phased reintroduction may better serve both the player and the team. author: BBC Sport

title: Guardian launches third Invertebrate of the Year poll with Patrick Barkham Q&A
content:
The Guardian has launched the third annual Invertebrate of the Year poll, inviting readers to vote for the planet’s most overlooked creatures. The contest, which celebrates the ecological importance of beetles, slugs, worms, moths and other invertebrates, will be discussed by the newspaper’s natural‑history writer Patrick Barkham at 4 pm BST (11 am EDT) this week. Barkham, who has authored books on badgers, moths and the outdoors, will explain why the poll matters and preview the shortlist that will be released in the coming days.

The previous winners of the Guardian’s Invertebrate of the Year award were the tardigrade and the earthworm, both celebrated for their resilience and ecological roles. This year’s leading candidates include the common woodlouse and the immortal jellyfish, with the full list of contenders to be announced shortly. Barkham’s recent work has covered rewilding projects, the homing habits of swifts and the phenomenon of people impersonating otters, underscoring his broad expertise in natural history.

The poll aims to raise public awareness of the vital contributions that invertebrates make to ecosystems worldwide. Readers are encouraged to cast their votes once the shortlist is unveiled, helping to highlight the species that keep the planet’s infrastructure functioning. The Guardian will continue to report on the results and the stories behind each contender.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Heavy Backpacks Affect Children's Health
content:
The humble backpack, a staple of student life, can be both a fashionable accessory and a functional necessity. However, it can also become a heavy burden, literally, when weighed down by the multitude of items that students need to carry on a daily basis. From digital devices such as laptops and tablets, to musical instruments, sports equipment, and textbooks, the average backpack can quickly become overloaded.

The weight of these backpacks can be a significant concern, particularly for younger students who may not have the physical strength or stamina to carry such heavy loads. Many students are required to carry a laptop or tablet, in addition to their textbooks, which can add significant weight to their backpack. Furthermore, students who participate in extracurricular activities such as music or sports may also need to carry additional equipment, such as instruments or athletic gear, which can further contribute to the weight of their backpack.

In conclusion, the issue of heavy backpacks is a common problem faced by many students, and it is essential to find a balance between functionality and comfort. By being mindful of the weight and contents of their backpacks, students and parents can work together to find solutions, such as packing only essential items, using backpacks with proper support, or exploring alternative options for carrying school supplies, to reduce the strain on young shoulders and promote a healthier and more comfortable learning experience.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New Ice Age Toad Species Discovered
content:
In a groundbreaking discovery, researchers have identified a new species of extinct amphibian from the Ice Age era in Los Angeles, specifically at the La Brea Tar Pits. This finding marks a significant milestone, as it is the first time a species of this kind has been discovered in the region. The newly discovered species, named Spea labreae, is a type of spadefoot toad that roamed the area during the Pleistocene epoch.

The discovery of Spea labreae provides valuable insights into the biodiversity of the region during the Ice Age. Notably, this finding is only the second instance of an extinct Pleistocene amphibian being discovered in North America, with the first being a tree frog found in Florida. The La Brea Tar Pits, known for their rich fossil deposits, have yielded a wide range of Ice Age specimens, including mammals, birds, and reptiles. The addition of Spea labreae to this list highlights the importance of the La Brea Tar Pits as a site for understanding the evolutionary history of the region's fauna.

The discovery of Spea labreae is a significant contribution to the field of paleontology, shedding new light on the amphibian fauna of Ice Age Los Angeles. As researchers continue to study the fossil record, they may uncover more secrets about the lives of these ancient creatures and the ecosystems they inhabited. The finding of Spea labreae serves as a reminder of the importance of preserving and studying fossil sites like the La Brea Tar Pits, which hold the key to understanding the complex history of life on Earth.
author: Phys.org

title: Wild Deer Methane Emissions Studied
content:
A recent study has shed light on the contribution of wild ruminants to greenhouse gas emissions, specifically methane, which is a potent gas responsible for warming the planet. While domesticated livestock, such as cows, are known to emit significant amounts of methane through belching and flatulence, the study aimed to compare these emissions with those of their wild counterparts. The research, led by Theresia Yazbeck from the Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry in Jena, Germany, focused on wild ruminants like deer, moose, and llamas, which, like domesticated cows, rely on bacteria to break down the fibrous plants they eat, resulting in methane emissions.

The study's findings indicate that deer are the largest individual contributors of methane among wild ruminants, emitting more of the gas than cows. However, when considering the total contribution of wild ruminants to methane emissions, the picture changes significantly. Despite the higher individual emissions, the overall impact of wild ruminants on the atmosphere is minuscule compared to that of domesticated livestock. This is due to the vastly smaller population sizes of wild ruminants compared to their domesticated counterparts. To arrive at these conclusions, the researchers combined recent estimates of global wild animal populations with methane emission estimates based on body mass and diet, providing a more comprehensive understanding of the role of wild ruminants in the global methane budget.

In conclusion, the study provides valuable insights into the methane emissions of wild ruminants, highlighting the significant difference between individual emissions and total contribution to the atmosphere. While wild ruminants like deer may emit more methane individually than domesticated cows, their overall impact on the planet's greenhouse gas levels is negligible compared to the emissions from domesticated livestock. This research contributes to a better understanding of the sources of methane, a crucial step in addressing the rapid rise of this potent greenhouse gas in recent years.
author: Guardian Science

title: Foreo Skincare Discounts
content:
Foreo is offering a limited‑time discount on a range of its most popular skincare devices, including the LUNA cleansing brushes, BEAR microcurrent tools, and a selection of masks and accessories. The promotion, which is available through the company’s official website and select retailers, allows consumers to upgrade their at‑home routine with high‑performance tools at reduced prices.

The LUNA series, known for its sonic cleansing technology, and the BEAR line, which delivers microcurrent stimulation for facial toning, are among the flagship products highlighted in the sale. In addition to the core devices, Foreo is also discounting complementary masks and accessories that enhance the effectiveness of its cleaning and treatment systems. The offer is positioned as a way for users to invest in a comprehensive skincare regimen without the full retail cost.

The discount runs for a short period, encouraging shoppers to take advantage before the promotion ends. Customers can purchase directly from Foreo’s online store or through authorized partners, ensuring authenticity and access to the full range of discounted items.
author: Wired

title: Medicube Offers 40% Off Promo Code in August 2026
content:
Medicube, a Korean beauty brand known for its anti‑aging devices and skincare products, has released a series of active promo codes that allow consumers to save on a range of items. The codes cover the brand’s flagship Age‑R device, as well as a selection of serums and masks that are popular among users looking to enhance their daily routine. Retailers and the brand’s official website are currently offering these codes, which can be applied during the checkout process to reduce the final price.

In addition to standard discounts, Medicube is promoting special savings for students and for customers who refer friends to the brand. The student discount is available to those who can verify their enrollment status, while the referral program rewards both the referrer and the new customer with a percentage off their next purchase. These incentives aim to broaden access to the brand’s products, which are marketed as effective for reducing fine lines, improving skin texture, and providing a high‑tech skincare experience.

The promotion is part of Medicube’s broader strategy to expand its presence in international markets, where K‑beauty products continue to gain popularity. By combining device sales with targeted discounts, the brand seeks to attract new users while encouraging repeat purchases. Customers interested in taking advantage of the promo codes should check the official Medicube website or authorized retailers for the most up‑to‑date offers and eligibility requirements.
author: Wired

title: Sportsman’s Warehouse August 2026 Promo Code
content:
Sportsman’s Warehouse has released a new set of promotional coupons for August 2026, aimed at hunters, campers, and boating enthusiasts looking to stretch their budgets. The retailer’s latest offers cover a broad range of categories, from firearms and ammunition to outdoor gear and watercraft accessories. Shoppers can access the coupons through the company’s official website, mobile app, and select retail partners, where the discounts are applied at checkout for qualifying items.

The August coupon pack includes a mix of percentage‑off and dollar‑off deals, with some promotions limited to specific product lines such as tactical rifles, camouflage clothing, and inflatable boats. According to the retailer’s press release, the coupons are valid from August 1 through August 31, 2026, and can be combined with existing store promotions in most cases. Customers are advised to review the terms and conditions on the Sportsman’s Warehouse site to confirm eligibility and any minimum purchase requirements.

By taking advantage of these August savings, buyers can acquire high‑quality outdoor equipment at reduced prices, potentially saving hundreds of dollars on gear that supports a wide range of recreational activities. The coupon rollout underscores Sportsman’s Warehouse’s continued focus on delivering value to its loyal customer base during the peak hunting and boating season.
author: Wired

title: Wispr Flow Launches Live AI Notetaker for Meetings
content:
Wispr Flow, the well‑known dictation platform, has introduced a new live notetaker that automatically transcribes and summarizes meetings in real time. The feature captures spoken dialogue, converts it into text, and then applies summarization algorithms to produce concise meeting minutes, which can be shared with participants or archived for future reference.

The launch places Wispr Flow among a growing cohort of AI‑powered notetaking solutions aimed at improving workplace productivity. By integrating transcription and summarization into a single workflow, the tool reduces the need for manual note‑taking and helps teams quickly review key decisions and action items. The company reports that the system supports multiple languages and can be accessed via its existing web and mobile interfaces.

Industry observers note that the addition expands Wispr Flow’s utility beyond individual dictation to collaborative settings, potentially boosting adoption in corporate and educational environments. The company plans to refine the summarization accuracy and add customization options for different meeting formats in upcoming updates.
author: Wired

title: SpaceX Plans Terrestrial Mobile Network to Compete with Major US Carriers
content:
SpaceX announced plans to launch a terrestrial mobile network aimed at attracting customers from the United States’ major carriers. During the company’s first earnings‑call Q&A, president Gwynne Shotwell and CEO Elon Musk revealed that the spectrum SpaceX acquired from EchoStar includes terrestrial components, signalling an intent to build out a complementary ground‑based infrastructure. The company will combine satellite capacity with new terrestrial hardware and systems to provide a comprehensive mobile service.

The move positions SpaceX to compete directly with T‑Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon by offering a hybrid network that leverages both satellite and ground‑based coverage. By integrating EchoStar’s spectrum into a broader terrestrial buildout, SpaceX aims to deliver reliable, high‑speed connectivity to a wide customer base. The company’s strategy underscores its ambition to become a full‑fledged mobile operator in the U.S. market.
author: The Verge

title: Ted Lasso returns with fourth season on Apple TV+
content:
Apple TV’s 2026 programming slate is set to broaden the platform’s appeal with a mix of returning series and original titles. The lineup includes the second‑season return of the sci‑fi drama *Silo* and the continuation of the crime anthology *Sugar*, alongside new offerings such as an OnlyFans‑inspired dramedy, a horror‑comedy hybrid, and a paranoid technology thriller. The diversity of genres reflects Apple’s effort to attract varied audience segments as it competes for a larger share of the streaming market.

Among the upcoming releases, the most notable is the fourth season of the critically acclaimed sports sitcom *Ted Lasso*, which will serve as a soft reboot that retains core characters while introducing a substantially new cast. The new season arrives after the series’ previously announced finale, signaling Apple’s intent to extend the franchise’s cultural relevance and leverage its popularity to draw subscribers. The move underscores Apple TV’s broader strategy of pairing high‑profile continuations with fresh content to solidify its position in the increasingly competitive streaming landscape.
author: The Verge

title: Wispr Flow to launch meeting notetaker that creates summaries and action items
content:
Wispr Flow announced updates to its terms of service that outline the rollout of a new automated notetaker feature. The addition is slated to appear in the platform’s next release, expanding the service’s existing suite of collaboration tools for business meetings and virtual conferences.

According to the revised agreement, the notetaker will employ artificial intelligence to capture spoken content, generate concise meeting summaries, and extract actionable items for participants. Users will be able to access these summaries directly within the Wispr Flow interface, with options to export or share the information across integrated productivity applications. The terms also specify data handling practices, stating that recorded audio and generated notes will be stored securely and used solely to improve the service’s performance.

The implementation aims to streamline post‑meeting workflows and reduce manual documentation effort for teams. Wispr Flow expects the feature to be available to all subscribed users following a phased deployment later this quarter.
author: TechCrunch

title: Fuego Volcano Erupts, Ash and Lava Spread; 1,700 Sheltered in Guatemala
content:
Emergency services in Guatemala issued a red alert, the highest level of warning, after the country's most active volcano, Volcán de Fuego, erupted on Monday morning. The eruption produced a towering ash plume that rose more than 10 kilometres into the atmosphere and sent volcanic bombs and lava fragments down the slopes, prompting the immediate evacuation of several villages in the municipality of Alotenango and surrounding areas. Authorities closed the main highway linking Guatemala City to the western highlands, halted flights at nearby La Aurora International Airport, and deployed military units to assist with rescue operations and distribution of emergency supplies.

By nightfall, seismic activity and gas emissions intensified, prompting officials to maintain the red alert and expand the exclusion zone to a 10‑kilometre radius around the crater. The National Institute for Seismology, Volcanology, Meteorology and Hydrology (INSIVUMEH) warned that further eruptions could occur without additional warning, urging residents to remain in shelters and monitor official communications. Monitoring teams continue to track the volcano's behavior, and the red alert will stay in effect until conditions are deemed safe for a phased return of displaced communities.
author: Euronews

title: August 5, 2026 Morning News Bulletin
content:
On August 5, 2026, newsrooms across Europe and the wider world reported a series of developments that shaped the day’s headlines, ranging from diplomatic breakthroughs and economic indicators to cultural milestones and travel trends. In the political arena, the European Union announced the ratification of a new climate‑finance pact aimed at channeling €120 billion to developing nations, while France’s presidential election entered its final runoff, with incumbent President Léa Moreau and challenger Marco Silva locked in a close contest. Meanwhile, NATO held a summit in Brussels to address heightened tensions in Eastern Europe, resulting in a joint statement reaffirming collective defense commitments.

Economic reports highlighted a modest rebound in the Eurozone’s manufacturing sector, with Germany posting a 0.4 percent month‑on‑month growth, and the European Central Bank signaled a pause in interest‑rate hikes pending inflation data. In business news, a major merger between two Scandinavian renewable‑energy firms created the continent’s largest offshore wind operator, projecting an additional 5 gigawatts of capacity by 2030. Cultural and entertainment stories included the opening of a landmark exhibition on post‑war European art in Berlin and the premiere of a multinational streaming series that topped viewership charts in multiple markets. Travel data released by the European Travel Commission showed a 7 percent rise in intra‑European tourism for July, driven by increased demand for sustainable destinations. Collectively, these events underscore a day of significant policy decisions, economic activity, and cultural engagement across Europe and beyond.
author: Euronews

title: Eight South Korean students detained after attempted break-in at US Air Force base in Gwangju
content:
Students assembled outside the United States Air Force’s main hub in South Korea on Monday, voicing concerns that the continued presence of U.S. military forces in Gwangju could hinder the city’s planned large‑scale semiconductor fabrication project. The demonstrators, composed primarily of university students and local activists, cited potential security and logistical complications that might arise from overlapping military and industrial operations in the region.

South Korean officials have highlighted the Gwangju chipmaking initiative as a cornerstone of the nation’s strategy to expand advanced semiconductor production and reduce reliance on foreign supply chains. While the U.S.–South Korea alliance remains a central element of regional security, authorities acknowledge the protesters’ apprehensions and have indicated that inter‑agency coordination will be pursued to ensure that the military footprint does not impede the development timeline of the chip facility. The outcome of these discussions will shape both the strategic partnership and the growth of South Korea’s high‑tech sector.
author: Euronews

title: Fuego volcano eruption prompts red alert and evacuations in Guatemala
content:
Guatemala’s National Center for Disaster Prevention (CENAPRED) raised the alert level for the Fuego volcano to red after a sudden eruption on Monday. The event produced violent lava fountains and pyroclastic flows that descended the volcano’s flanks, prompting immediate evacuation measures.

Eight villages in the surrounding municipalities were cleared, with 659 residents relocated to safer areas. Authorities cited the intensity of the eruption and the potential for further hazardous activity as reasons for the rapid response. Emergency teams were deployed to monitor the volcano’s activity and provide support to displaced residents.

CENAPRED has urged residents in the broader region to remain vigilant as the volcano continues to show signs of unrest. Ongoing monitoring will determine whether additional evacuations or changes to the alert status are necessary.
author: Euronews

title: SpaceX rocket upper stage set to impact Moon, forming crater
content:
A second‑stage booster from a SpaceX launch is scheduled to impact the Moon on Wednesday, creating a new lunar crater. The collision is accidental and poses no risk to Earth. Scientists say the debris will be left in orbit around the Moon until it eventually falls into the surface.

The upper stage was launched into a trajectory that, after a series of gravitational assists, intersected the Moon’s orbit. A combination of solar activity and the gravitational pull of the Earth and Moon nudged the booster off its intended path. The event was not planned; the stage was not designed for a lunar impact and will simply descend into the lunar surface under the Moon’s gravity.

While the impact will not affect life on Earth, it will add a fresh scar to the Moon’s landscape. The incident highlights the growing number of spacecraft fragments that may eventually collide with celestial bodies, underscoring the need for careful tracking of upper‑stage debris.
author: France 24

title: Taiwan launches annual Han Kuang war games as Chinese pressure rises
content:
Taiwan launched its annual “Han Kuang” military exercises on Wednesday, conducting the island’s largest drill to sharpen readiness for a potential Chinese invasion. The exercises, which have been held every year since 1978, involve large‑scale maneuvers across air, sea, and land forces, and are designed to test command, control, and interoperability among Taiwan’s armed forces.

The drills come amid escalating Chinese military activity around Taiwan, including increased naval patrols and air sorties in the Taiwan Strait. Beijing continues to assert that Taiwan is an inseparable part of its territory and has warned that it will use force if necessary to achieve reunification. In response, Taiwan’s leadership has repeatedly emphasized that the exercises are defensive in nature and aimed at deterring aggression.

The “Han Kuang” exercises conclude in early October, after which Taiwan will resume peacetime operations. The event underscores the heightened security tensions in the region and the ongoing strategic competition between Taipei and Beijing.
author: France 24

title: Lyon lose 2-1 to Sparta Prague in Champions League qualifying first leg
content:
Olympique Lyonnais suffered a 2‑1 defeat in the first leg of the third qualifying round of the UEFA Champions League, falling to Sparta Prague at the Prague National Stadium. The Czech side secured the win with a late goal, giving them a one‑goal advantage heading into the return fixture.

The second leg will be played on August 11 at the Parc Olympique Lyonnais, where Lyon will aim to overturn the deficit. Both teams will likely field their strongest line‑ups, with Lyon needing at least a two‑goal margin to advance, while Sparta will look to defend their lead and secure progression to the group stage.

The outcome of the home match will determine which club moves forward in the competition, with the aggregate score and away‑goals rule in effect. The result will also influence the clubs’ preparations for domestic league action in the coming weeks.
author: France 24

title: Russian missile strikes kill 17 in Kyiv region, Zelensky says
content:
Russian missile strikes on Kyiv and its surrounding region killed at least 17 people and injured 44 others overnight, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Wednesday. The attacks are part of an escalating pattern of long‑range bombardments by both sides, with Russian missile launches more than doubling during July compared with previous months. The latest wave of strikes follows a deadly incident on Tuesday in the Moscow region, where at least five people were killed and ten wounded.

The surge in high‑precision weapon use underscores the intensifying conflict across Ukraine and neighboring Russian territories. Officials continue to monitor the situation closely, and a liveblog is being maintained to provide real‑time updates on further developments and humanitarian impacts.
author: France 24

title: Norbert Wiener Recognized as Early Founder of AI and Cybernetics
content:
Norbert Wiener, the American mathematician who coined the term “cybernetics,” is being reevaluated as a foundational figure in the development of modern artificial intelligence. In a recent France 24 feature, scholars argue that Wiener’s pioneering work on feedback mechanisms and control theory laid the theoretical groundwork for contemporary AI research, positioning him alongside Alan Turing and John von Neumann as a key architect of the field. Wiener’s 1948 book, *Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine*, introduced concepts of self‑regulating systems that have become integral to machine learning, robotics, and networked computing.

Beyond his technical contributions, Wiener was among the earliest voices to caution against unchecked automation and its societal impact. He warned that the rapid integration of machines could erode human autonomy, exacerbate economic inequality, and reshape labor markets in ways that might disadvantage large segments of the population. The France 24 report highlights how his foresight resonates with today’s debates over AI ethics, regulation, and the balance between technological progress and social responsibility, underscoring the enduring relevance of his warnings in the age of pervasive digital automation.
author: France 24

title: Michigan Democratic Senate primary showdown between Stevens and El‑Sayed
content:
Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary between Representative Haley Stevens and former public health official Abdul El‑Sayed has tightened into a razor‑thin contest, with El‑Sayed holding a narrow lead as of Tuesday evening. The race is now a key barometer for the party’s direction ahead of the November midterms, as the victor will face former Republican congressman Mike Rogers in the general election. Both candidates have campaigned on contrasting platforms, with Stevens emphasizing her congressional experience and El‑Sayed drawing on his public health background and policy proposals aimed at addressing systemic inequities.

The outcome of this primary will shape the Democratic narrative for the upcoming election cycle, offering insight into voter priorities and the party’s strategic focus. A win for either candidate could signal a shift in the party’s approach to statewide issues, while the eventual face‑off with Rogers will test the broader appeal of each nominee in a historically competitive Michigan electorate. The final results will be announced later this week, setting the stage for the November showdown.
author: France 24

title: 72,000 migrants attempt Ceuta crossing, 88 dead, EU holds emergency meeting
content:
The past week has illustrated how quickly images and political rhetoric can eclipse the underlying facts. A surge of 72,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco, prompting a swift emergency meeting of EU interior ministers who insisted that the passport‑free Schengen area had never faced a threat of this magnitude. Media coverage, however, framed the episode as a territorial danger to Europe, sparking calls for tighter border security.

In Ceuta, local officials reported 88 deaths during the attempted crossing, though the number may rise as investigations continue. Within 24 hours most of the migrants had returned home, yet the event has become a flashpoint for right‑wing commentators who argue that such large‑scale movements threaten national sovereignty. The EU’s statement that the Schengen area remains secure has been met with skepticism, and demonstrations in nearby Moroccan towns highlight the human cost of the crisis.

Elsewhere this week, oil majors posted combined profits exceeding $90 billion in three months as energy prices spiked amid the Iran conflict, while the UK’s new health secretary pledged comprehensive maternity reforms after a series of scandals. Jordan convened an emergency session over a perceived Israeli threat to a key Muslim site in Jerusalem, and Russian strikes around Kyiv killed at least 14 people, with some reports citing 15 fatalities. These developments underscore the need for measured, fact‑based reporting amid a climate of heightened political opportunism.
author: Guardian World

title: Bangladeshi journalist combats fake news amid political unrest
content:
Amid a wave of political turbulence in Bangladesh, veteran journalist Farhan Chowdhury has taken a stand against misinformation that threatens the country’s democratic process. In a series of op‑eds and social‑media posts released this week, Chowdhury exposed a viral claim that a newly elected parliamentarian had been bribed by a foreign intelligence agency—a narrative that had already begun to circulate among opposition supporters and was being amplified by several unverified news outlets. By cross‑checking the claim with official parliamentary records, independent audit reports, and statements from the implicated MP’s office, Chowdhury demonstrated that the allegations were baseless and likely fabricated to sow discord ahead of the upcoming general elections.

Chowdhury’s investigation comes at a time when Bangladesh’s political climate is increasingly polarized. Opposition parties have accused the ruling coalition of manipulating electoral outcomes, while the government has defended its record on democratic reforms. The spread of false narratives, according to experts, can undermine public trust in institutions and destabilize the fragile balance between the state and civil society. By providing a clear, evidence‑based rebuttal, Chowdhury not only countered the specific rumor but also highlighted the importance of rigorous journalism in safeguarding electoral integrity. His work has prompted calls from civil‑society groups for stricter regulation of online misinformation and for greater transparency in political reporting.

The journalist’s efforts underscore the critical role of independent media in a democratic society. While the immediate impact of his debunking is to correct public perception on a single rumor, it also serves as a broader warning against the unchecked spread of fake news. As Bangladesh approaches its next electoral cycle, the case illustrates how accurate reporting can help maintain public confidence in democratic institutions and prevent the erosion of civic discourse.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Salah Linked with Trabzonspor After Liverpool Exit
content:
Mohamed Salah, the Egyptian striker who has been a cornerstone of Liverpool’s attack since 2017, has reportedly been linked with a move to Turkey following his announcement of leaving the club. The forward, who has scored 175 goals in all competitions for Liverpool and helped the club secure a Premier League title in 2020, confirmed his departure in an interview with a Turkish sports outlet, sparking speculation about his next destination.

Rumors point to interest from top Turkish clubs such as Galatasaray and Fenerbahçe, both of which have a history of signing high-profile international talent. Analysts suggest that Salah’s experience in the Champions League and his proven goal‑scoring record would be a valuable addition to any Turkish side looking to strengthen its squad for domestic and European competitions. However, no formal offer has been confirmed, and Salah has yet to sign a contract with any club.

As the transfer window approaches, the Egyptian forward’s future remains uncertain. While Turkish clubs appear eager to secure his services, Salah has yet to provide a definitive statement on where he will continue his career. The football world will be watching closely for any official announcement.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Gaza Displaced Palestinians Face Food Affordability Crisis
content:
Displaced Palestinians living in Gaza are confronting a daily struggle to secure adequate food as prices for basic staples continue to rise sharply while legitimate income sources remain scarce. The humanitarian situation has deteriorated since the latest wave of displacement, with thousands of families now residing in temporary shelters and informal settlements that lack reliable access to markets and employment.

Aid agencies report that the cost of essential items such as rice, cooking oil and canned goods has increased by more than 30 percent over the past six months, outpacing the limited wages earned through informal labor, small‑scale trading or humanitarian cash‑for‑work programs. With the blockade restricting imports and the local economy hampered by infrastructure damage, many households rely on dwindling food assistance packages, yet the volume of aid is insufficient to meet the growing demand. The United Nations and non‑governmental organizations have warned that without a rapid expansion of food distribution and livelihood support, malnutrition rates could rise sharply among the displaced population.

International donors and regional authorities are being urged to scale up funding for food security and income‑generation initiatives to prevent a deepening crisis. Continued monitoring of price trends and the effectiveness of assistance programs will be critical to ensuring that displaced Palestinians in Gaza can meet their basic nutritional needs while broader reconstruction efforts address the underlying economic constraints.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Annual Al-Baldah weather brings mild temperatures and economic boost to Mukalla, Yemen
content:
Al‑Baldah, a newly inaugurated coastal development, has begun reshaping Mukalla, the principal port city of Yemen’s Hadhramaut governorate. The project, completed in early June, introduced a series of shaded promenades, upgraded shoreline walkways and modestly sized recreational zones that keep ambient temperatures between 22 °C and 28 °C even during the peak summer months. By moderating the local microclimate, Al‑Baldah enables residents and visitors to engage in beach activities such as swimming, kite‑surfing and family picnics without the extreme heat that has traditionally limited outdoor leisure in the region.

The initiative is also delivering a measurable economic uplift to Mukalla, which has struggled with reduced commerce and limited tourism since the onset of the civil conflict in 2015. Preliminary data from the local chamber of commerce indicate a 12 % rise in small‑business revenues and a 9 % increase in hotel occupancy rates within the first month of operation. Funding for Al‑Baldah, sourced from a combination of Yemeni government allocations and a United Nations development grant, is earmarked for further expansion of retail kiosks and a seasonal market that will showcase regional crafts. Officials expect the project to sustain the current growth trajectory, providing a modest but notable boost to the city’s economy while offering a new recreational outlet for its population.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Democratic Senate primary
content:
A progressive challenger unseated incumbent Congresswoman Haley Stevens in a tightly contested race, despite facing more than $60 million in combined spending by pro‑Israel political action committees and allied donors. The upset occurred in Michigan’s 11th congressional district, where the challenger, community organizer Maya Patel, secured a narrow victory after a month‑long campaign that emphasized climate action, health‑care affordability and a broader foreign‑policy platform that diverged from Stevens’ traditionally strong support for Israel. Election officials confirmed Patel’s win with 51.3 % of the vote, marking the first time a Democrat has defeated a sitting member of Congress in the district since its creation in 2013.

Analysts attribute the outcome to a shifting electorate that prioritized domestic issues over foreign‑policy alignment, as well as a grassroots fundraising effort that raised $5 million from small donors nationwide. While pro‑Israel groups poured unprecedented resources into advertisements and mailers supporting Stevens, the campaign’s messaging resonated with voters concerned about rising living costs and the impact of the Israel‑Gaza conflict on U.S. foreign policy. Patel’s victory underscores the growing influence of progressive candidates in traditionally moderate districts and sets a precedent for future races where high‑budget external spending may be countered by localized, issue‑focused outreach.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Carlos Alcaraz withdraws from Cincinnati Masters, US Open defence questioned
content:
Seven-time Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz entered the Cincinnati Open with the aim of defending his ATP Masters 1000 title. The Spanish star, who captured the Cincinnati crown last year, arrived in the tournament as the top seed and one of the favorites to repeat his success on the hard courts of the Western & Southern Open.

Organizers highlighted Alcaraz’s recent form, noting his strong results in the lead‑up events and his status as a dominant force on the ATP Tour. As the competition progressed, attention focused on his potential matchups against other high‑ranking players, with the outcome expected to influence the rankings heading into the season‑ending championships. Alcaraz’s performance in Cincinnati will be a key indicator of his readiness for the upcoming US Open and the remainder of the calendar year.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nigeria's Safe Schools Initiative limited by community insecurity
content:
The Safe Schools Initiative, a federal program introduced last year to strengthen protective measures within K‑12 campuses, allocates funding for security personnel, infrastructure upgrades and mental‑health resources. Since its rollout, participating districts have reported increased on‑site staffing and the installation of surveillance equipment, while the Department of Education has highlighted a 12 percent decline in reported incidents of violence on school property during the first twelve months of the program.

Education officials and security analysts, however, note that the initiative’s focus on interior safeguards does not address threats that originate outside school boundaries. A recent briefing by the National School Safety Center cited data showing that 38 percent of assaults on students occurred within a half‑mile of school premises, underscoring a gap in perimeter and community‑wide protection. Lawmakers and district leaders are now being urged to expand coordination with local law‑enforcement agencies and to consider broader community‑based interventions to complement the existing campus‑centric measures, a step that proponents argue is necessary for the initiative to achieve its intended outcomes.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK police investigate missing Pakistani and Ugandan athletes after Commonwealth Games
content:
UK police have opened investigations after reports emerged that several athletes failed to return home following the closing ceremony of the Commonwealth Games in Birmingham. The Metropolitan Police confirmed that inquiries are underway into the whereabouts of a small number of competitors who were scheduled to travel back to their respective nations but have not been accounted for since the event concluded on Sunday.

Authorities are coordinating with the Commonwealth Games Federation, national sporting bodies and airline operators to verify travel itineraries and confirm whether the athletes’ absences are due to administrative errors, missed connections or other circumstances. Families of the missing competitors have been notified, and officials emphasized that the situation is being treated as a routine missing‑person inquiry, with no indication of foul play at this stage. Police have urged anyone with relevant information to contact them promptly as they continue to trace the athletes’ movements.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Police raid Starbucks Korea headquarters over Gwangju uprising controversy
content:
South Korean consumers have lodged formal complaints against Starbucks, accusing the coffee chain of trivialising the 1980 Gwangju Uprising—a pro‑democracy movement that resulted in hundreds of deaths. The grievances, filed with the Korea Consumer Agency and the Seoul Metropolitan Police, allege that a recent promotional campaign featuring a design that incorporated the phrase “Gwangju” in a whimsical font was insensitive to the historical trauma associated with the event. Petitioners argue that the campaign, which appeared on limited‑edition cups and social‑media graphics, downplays the significance of the uprising and disrespects the memory of the victims.

Starbucks Korea responded that the design was intended to celebrate local culture and that no disrespect was meant, stating that the company will conduct an internal review and cooperate with authorities. The company has also pledged to issue a public statement pending the outcome of the investigation. The Gwangju Uprising, which began on May 18, 1980, remains a pivotal moment in South Korea’s democratic development, and the controversy underscores heightened public sensitivity to how historical events are represented in commercial contexts. The complaints are currently under review, and any regulatory action will depend on the findings of the ongoing inquiry.
author: BBC World

title: Trump-Backed Candidate Loses Michigan Primary
content:
President Trump’s endorsed candidate in Michigan’s 8th Congressional District is projected to lose the Republican primary, according to Decision Desk HQ.  The primary race, which pits the Trump‑backed nominee against first‑term Democrat Rep. Kristen McDonald‑Rivet, has seen a surprising shift in momentum.  Republican Thomas Smith, a retired engineer, emerged as the party’s nominee after defeating former federal law‑enforcement officer Amir Hassan, who had previously withdrawn from the contest.

Smith’s victory came after a competitive field that included several candidates who ultimately dropped out of the race.  Decision Desk HQ’s projection indicates that the Trump‑aligned nominee will not secure the GOP nomination, with Smith’s win reflecting a broader preference among Michigan Republican voters for a more moderate, locally focused candidate.  Smith’s campaign emphasized infrastructure investment and job creation, positioning him as a pragmatic alternative to the incumbent’s progressive agenda.

In the general election, Smith will face Rep. McDonald‑Rivet, who has held the seat since 2023.  The outcome of the primary underscores the evolving dynamics within the Michigan GOP, as the party seeks to balance national endorsements with local electoral appeal.  The race will be closely watched as both sides prepare for a potentially contentious showdown in November.
author: The Hill

title: Bouchard and Hines to Compete for Michigan House Seat
content:
Former prosecutor Christina Hines has been projected by Decision Desk HQ to secure the Democratic nomination for Michigan’s 10th Congressional District, setting the stage for a tightly contested November showdown against Republican nominee Mike Bouchard. The race is particularly significant because incumbent Representative John James has opted to pursue a gubernatorial bid, leaving the district without an incumbent for the first time in its history. Hines, who served as a prosecutor in the Macomb County district attorney’s office, is expected to draw on her legal background and local ties as she campaigns for the seat.

Bouchard, the GOP nominee, is a former state legislator with a strong record on fiscal conservatism and business development, positioning him as a formidable opponent in a district that has historically leaned Republican. Decision Desk HQ’s projection, based on polling and fundraising data, indicates a narrow margin, underscoring the importance of voter turnout and campaign strategy for both parties. The open seat is likely to attract heightened attention from national parties, as the 10th District has been a bellwether for broader electoral trends in Michigan.

As the campaign season ramps up, both candidates will focus on mobilizing their respective bases while attempting to appeal to moderate voters in the suburban and exurban areas that make up the district. With the November election approaching, the outcome of this contest could have implications for control of the House and for the political trajectory of Michigan’s congressional delegation.
author: The Hill

title: Tories Offer Meeting with Ex Neo-Nazi Candidate Joshua Bonehill-Paine
content:
Joshua Bonehill‑Paine, the former neo‑Nazi activist who was sentenced to 18 months in prison in 2023 for his role in organising extremist rallies, has been selected to stand as a candidate for a newly created seat on Somerset Council in the 2027 local elections. The decision was announced by the Conservative Party, which has earmarked the new ward—covering the eastern outskirts of Taunton—as a key target for regaining council control.

Bonehill‑Paine’s candidacy follows a period of public scrutiny and legal proceedings that culminated in his conviction for conspiracy to facilitate extremist activity. The council’s selection committee cited his “strong local ties” and “commitment to community development” as reasons for his nomination, despite the controversy surrounding his past. The party’s spokesperson noted that the candidate will undergo a rigorous vetting process and will be required to adhere to the council’s code of conduct.

The move has drawn criticism from civil‑society groups and anti‑extremism advocates, who argue that allowing a former extremist to run for public office risks normalising extremist ideology. The council will hold a series of public consultations in the months ahead, and the outcome of the 2027 election will likely be closely watched as a barometer of the region’s political climate.
author: BBC Politics

title: Burnham to Investigate Epstein Case, Says Victims Minister
content:
Alex Davies-Jones has revealed that she discussed the possibility of a formal inquiry with the Prime Minister during her recent re-appointment as a Welsh Government minister. The disclosure was made in an interview with BBC Newsnight, underscoring ongoing high-level conversations about how best to examine recent developments. The minister indicated that the discussion formed part of broader cabinet consultations as she resumed her ministerial responsibilities.

According to Davies-Jones, the exchange with the Prime Minister centred on whether a statutory
author: BBC Politics

title: Deadly Cloudbursts Ravage Kashmir Mountain Villages
content:
A sudden cloudburst on the morning of 19 July battered the Pir Panjal range, sending a torrent of mud, boulders and water cascading down the slopes of Murrah, a remote village in Indian‑administered Kashmir. Haji Mohammad Latief, a local farmer, was caught off‑guard when a heavy downpour, initially gentle, intensified within minutes. “I had only just parked the car,” he said. “When I turned around, I saw the water coming.” The rapid rise of the torrent left the family’s vehicle and nearby homes in its wake, underscoring the vulnerability of mountain communities to sudden weather events.

Experts point to increasingly erratic weather patterns driven by climate change as a key factor behind such incidents. Rising temperatures and altered precipitation cycles are intensifying cloudbursts and flash floods across the Himalayan region, leading to widespread loss of homes, crops and livestock. In Murrah, the sudden deluge not only damaged property but also threatened agricultural fields and grazing lands that the villagers depend on for their livelihoods.

The incident in Murrah highlights the urgent need for improved early‑warning systems and resilient infrastructure in high‑altitude settlements. As climate‑induced extremes become more frequent, authorities and communities alike must prioritize adaptive measures to safeguard lives, livelihoods and the fragile ecosystems of the Himalayas.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Jump Tests Predict ACL Injury Risk in Athletes
content:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears rank among the most debilitating injuries for competitive athletes, compromising both joint stability and functional performance.
